## How Do LLMs Work? Transformers Explained (2026)
Large language models work by predicting the next token in a sequence, trained on trillions of examples of human text. A token is a word or sub-word unit — the word "understanding" might be split into "under" + "stand" + "ing." The model sees a sequence of tokens, computes probability distributions over its entire vocabulary (typically 100,000-200,000 tokens), and selects the most likely continuation. This process repeats, one token at a time, until the response is complete. [...] That last row matters more than it looks. At the very end of the network, only the last vector in the sequence is multiplied by the unembedding matrix to produce the next-token distribution. Every other vector in the final layer is "wasted" at inference time — but during training, every position predicts its own next token in parallel, which is what makes the math tractable on trillion-token corpora. ### Embedd

## What Is RLHF & How Does It Work? | Mercor
Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is a three-stage post-training method that involves supervised fine-tuning (SFT), reward model training, and reinforcement learning optimization. It's the reason ChatGPT behaves like an assistant instead of an autocomplete engine. The reward model is the most consequential piece. It turns human preference judgments into a trainable signal, and the quality of these judgments determines model quality more than pipeline architecture does. [...] The RLHF pipeline has three stages. First, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) teaches the model a task format. Second, a reward model learns to score outputs based on how humans ranked them. Third, reinforcement learning, typically using proximal policy optimization (PPO), improves the model's responses while keeping it from drifting too far from the fine-tuned version. There are mainly 3 steps involved in building ChatGPT- 1. Pretraining LLM 2. Supervised Finetuning of LLM (SFT) 3. Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) The first step is to pretrain the LLM (GPT 3.5) on the unsupervised data to predict the next word in the sentence. This makes LLM learn the representation and various nuances of the text. [...] In the next step, we finetune the LLM on the demonstration data: a dataset with the questions and answers. This optimizes the LLM for dialogue. In the final step, we use RLHF to control the responses generated by the LLM. We are prioritizing the better responses generated by the model using RLHF. ## RLHF in Generative AI: Definition & How It Works | Annotation Academy
Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) is the training technique that teaches AI models to generate responses humans prefer by ranking outputs and rewarding behaviors that match human judgment. RLHF transformed base language models like GPT-3 into conversational tools like ChatGPT by training models to follow instructions, refuse harmful requests, and produce helpful responses. This approach uses human evaluators to rank model outputs, trains a reward model to predict preferences, [...] Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) trains models on input-output pairs where humans provide the correct answer, while RLHF trains on ranked comparisons where humans indicate which output is better. SFT requires experts to write ideal responses for every training example; RLHF requires evaluators to compare model-generated responses, a faster and more practical task. ## How ChatGPT actually works | AssemblyAI
The creators have used a combination of both Supervised Learning and Reinforcement Learning to fine-tune ChatGPT, but it is the Reinforcement Learning component specifically that makes ChatGPT unique. The creators use a particular technique called Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), which uses human feedback in the training loop to minimize harmful, untruthful, and/or biased outputs.

plan.title: How ChatGPT Works: Predicting One Token at a Time
plan.description: Large language models like ChatGPT work by predicting the next token, trained on trillions of examples of text. This video explains tokens, transformers, attention and the human feedback that turns an autocomplete engine into an assistant.

beats.narration: ChatGPT has no plan for what it will say. It does not know how your answer ends when it starts. It just guesses one small piece of text, then guesses again.

props.text: It has no plan. It only predicts the next piece of text.

beats.narration: Those pieces are called tokens. A token is a word or part of a word. The word understanding might be split into under, stand, and ing.
Picture a researcher at a computer, feeding in enormous amounts of writing. The model trains on trillions of examples of human text, always practicing one task: guess what comes next.
Every guess starts as a score for each token in the vocabulary, typically one hundred thousand to two hundred thousand of them. Then the most likely continuation gets picked.

props.label: possible tokens scored for every single guess

beats.narration: First, tokens become numbers plus position, so the model knows word order. Then attention blocks mix in context. Finally, next-token odds come out, one probability for every token.
Attention lets each token look back at the earlier ones and gather context. A causal mask blocks any peeking ahead, so the model can only use what came before.
Training is a giant game of fill in the blank. The model guesses, the loss function measures the error, and backpropagation nudges millions of parameters to make better guesses next time.
After enough rounds, something remarkable emerges. By predicting the next word over billions of tokens, the model picks up grammar, word meanings, facts, and long-range connections between ideas.
To write a reply, it picks a token, adds it to the prompt, and runs everything again. New attention, new odds, new token. Repeat until the answer is done.
A dial called temperature controls how adventurous the pick is. Low means safe, predictable words. High means more surprising ones. That is why the same question can get different answers.
But a model that only predicts text is just autocomplete. The raw version, called a base model, may ramble on instead of answering your question.
So there are three steps. First, pretraining on raw text. Second, supervised fine-tuning on questions and answers. Third, reinforcement learning from human feedback, or RLHF.
In RLHF, people rank the model's answers. A reward model learns those preferences and scores new replies. The chatbot is then tuned toward answers humans prefer, and away from harmful ones.
So ChatGPT is a next-token predictor, shaped by human judgment. Every sentence it writes is one careful guess, repeated. That is all it takes to sound like it understands.
